summary: Ñawi ("eye" in Quechua) is an open web viewer that lets anyone step through real infrared images from NASA's SPHEREx telescope, see how objects move over time, and check how reliable each measurement is.
details:
Ñawi turns SPHEREx data into something anyone can explore. You choose an object, and Ñawi shows real SPHEREx cutouts, date by date, like a time machine:

  • Gallery of 5 test objects: Barnard's Star, RW Aurigae, R Draconis, WISE 0855-0714 and Epsilon Indi B.
  • Timeline with a slider, autoplay and previous/next frame buttons.
  • Before and after: a sliding comparison with the previous frame.
  • Expected-position marker and trajectory, computed from each object's proper motion.
  • Rastro (trace): how far the object moved, measured on the images and compared with the published value, with a plain-language sentence.
  • Latido (heartbeat): brightness curve for variable stars, showing the wavelength of every point.
  • Shareable view: the link stores the object and the frame.
  • Honest warnings: weak signal, saturated core, no data, backend unavailable. The interface never fills gaps or invents numbers.
